The same script then computes the induced affine toric data on every face and confirms that the piecewise action map glues on all 35 internal edges with exact zero midpoint jump. The full report was saved to `results/research_loop/attempt_011_exact_strip_gluing.json`.
did_not_work: The exactification does not make the proposed solution correct. The toric gluing audit shows that all 35 internal shared edges have midpoints strictly inside `Delta(1)`, so each carries a full `T^2` fiber, but `same_angle_matrix_count = 0`: no adjacent pair has matching `A^{-T}`. In fact the 36 faces carry 36 distinct action matrices. Because constant angle translations cannot repair a nonzero linear mismatch on a full torus fiber, the boundary-only strip is still not a continuous 4D toric piecewise-affine symplectic embedding. So the current hybrid family still does not solve the task.

patterns_noticed: Several strong exact patterns emerged. First, the optimizer's near-miss from attempt 010 was hiding a genuinely exact rational object: among all seeds with denominator at most 72, the recurrence has a unique root at `17/36`, and that seed forces `x_9 = 1` and `y_19 = 1` exactly. Second, the source strip is no longer an approximate area fit at all: every face has oriented double area exactly `1/36`, so the action-space equal-area equations are solved completely. Third, the internal-edge geometry is uniformly nondegenerate from the toric point of view: every one of the 35 shared-edge midpoints satisfies `x1 > 0`, `x2 > 0`, and `x1 + x2 < 1`, so each edge carries the full two-angle torus and there is no boundary-collapse escape hatch. Fourth, once the boundary vertex map is fixed, action continuity is automatic on a shared edge because the two affine face maps agree at the edge endpoints, and the report confirms exact zero action jump on all 35 edges. Fifth, the obstruction has therefore shifted entirely into the angular linear data: all 36 faces have distinct affine action matrices, and adjacent faces never share the same `A^{-T}`. On a full torus fiber that means continuity would force a single global affine matrix on the whole connected strip, so the current boundary-only non-triangular target shape cannot arise inside this toric piecewise-affine class. Finally, the exact recurrence shows an asymmetric but structured boundary pattern: the left BC parameters `y_1,...,y_8` collapse to repeated-numerator rational families while the right ladder reproduces the simple fractions already seen in scratch, suggesting the recurrence is rigid enough to certify exact witnesses but not rich enough to fix the 4D gluing defect by itself.
